context: area: frontend privileged application, player client, generated assets, build graph, embeds, scripts, and tests
constraint: preserve separate trusted Overseer and untrusted client runtime bundles
constraint: historical completed specs and rollback records remain unchanged
intent: Consolidate both frontend applications under one role-oriented frontend tree and establish Overseer as the canonical privileged UI identity without behavioral change.
expectations: No interface redesign or behavior change.
No unrelated backend wire or persisted-data contract migration.
No rewrite of completed historical specs or rollback records.
approach: Create one npm workspace under frontend with isolated client and overseer packages, move generated assets and independent dist roots with them, and update every active path consumer in one no-alias cutover. Preserve the public/private embed boundary and all runtime behavior.

decisions.decision: Use one npm workspace with client and overseer application members
decisions.why: One lockfile expresses common frontend ownership while role roots preserve independent builds

decisions.decision: Keep distinct client and Overseer production bundles and embeds
decisions.why: Preserves the simplest auditable public/private capability boundary

decisions.decision: Rename active privileged frontend and host terminology without migrating unrelated stable backend contracts
decisions.why: Satisfies the canonical Overseer identity without unrelated API churn

decisions.decision: Cut over all active paths without aliases
decisions.why: Prevents generators, CI, and tests from recreating a dual layout

decisions.decision: Preserve stable backend Master* domain contract identifiers while renaming the privileged frontend, host window, fixtures, assets, and visible terminology to Overseer.
decisions.why: The request targets frontend ownership and role identity; preserving internal serialized/API names avoids an unrelated breaking contract migration.
decisions.rejected: Renaming every backend domain type and wire-facing field in the same structural refactor.
